chapter: Union, publishers, race and Harlem nightlife
title: Friendship among musicians and Johnny Hodges
summary: He has friendships with all musicians except for a little resentment, and says Hodges had a big head.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Did you have some kind of friendship all over among the musicians, I mean like if something happened would everybody get together and discuss it or something like that?

I think, in my opinion. Now if I'm wrong, I'm sorry, but I have friendship with all musicians, all, all. One I kind of resented; I told you who he was, but that was nothing. That doesn't mean a thing. People are jealous sometimes. Talking about Jay Jay, you know. But that doesn't mean anything. I like him just like I do other musicians. The only guy that had a little head on him was Johnny Hodge's.
Yeah, he's kind of rough to get along with.
Kind of rough up here in the head, had a big head.
Tell me, did the musicians ever get together and did you have any kind of a club or anything?
You mean a special club? No, you could just find a place to hang out and go and take your horn and sit down and laugh and talk, play cards, drink whiskey...
Didn't you used to have jam sessions?
Sometimes they would last until 11 or 12 o'clock the next day.
